name: Community membership and price intelligence
demand: No verified search volume, installs, buyer count, or paid-user count found; those are unverified. Supply-side proxies only: on 23 Oct 2026, Check the Course reported 9,448 listings, 402,777 communities/products read in the last 28 days, and 1,252,883 readings across 10 weeks. Its Skool benchmark covers 2,127 listings with monthly prices. Skool Stats claims 121k+ communities and Playbuuk claims 71.9k+; both are vendor-reported coverage, not independent market counts or evidence of buyers. (https://checkthecourse.com/ ; https://checkthecourse.com/reports/skool-pricing-benchmarks ; https://www.skoolstats.com/ ; https://playbuuk.com/)
prices: Current alternatives: Skool Analytics advertises free access with no card; Skool Stats lists €149/month; an Apify Skool scraper lists pricing from $2.50 per 1,000 profiles. Skool’s own platform plans are $9/month and $99/month, and its admin analytics are a substitute for owners monitoring their own groups. Check the Course API/subscription price is unverified. Prices are not evidence of sales. (https://www.skoolanalytics.com/ ; https://www.skoolstats.com/pricing ; https://apify.com/vnx0/skool-community-scraper ; https://www.skool.com/pricing ; https://help.skool.com/article/216-analytics-definitions ; https://checkthecourse.com/)
copy_speed: There is already direct overlap: Check the Course publishes dated membership/price histories and benchmark reports; Skool Analytics tracks daily membership, prices, and activity; Skool Stats and Playbuuk offer cross-community intelligence. New-competitor evidence since April: AINave lists Skool Stats on 13 Oct 2026, while its actual launch date is unverified; the Apify scraper page said “published 5 days ago” when checked on 23 Oct (approximately 18 Oct), but its actual launch date is also unverified. (https://checkthecourse.com/reports ; https://www.skoolanalytics.com/ ; https://ainave.com/products/skool-stats ; https://www.skoolstats.com/pricing ; https://playbuuk.com/ ; https://apify.com/vnx0/skool-community-scraper)
platform_risk: High for a product sourced from Skool. Its terms prohibit commercial use and compiling directories from its content, and prohibit robots, crawlers, extraction software, and automated scraping or monitoring. Check the Course says its crawler reads pages allowed by robots.txt; that statement does not establish Skool’s permission. Build on Skool data only with confirmed authorization or a permitted feed. Public owner information can also be personal data: ICO guidance says public availability does not remove UK data-protection obligations. (https://www.skool.com/legal?t=terms ; https://checkthecourse.com/about ; https://checkthecourse.com/methodology ; https://ico.org.uk/media/about-the-ico/documents/4026232/joint-statement-data-scraping-202308.pdf)
defensible_asset: A source-linked longitudinal dataset could become useful, but the moat is weak as proposed: Check the Course already reports 10 weeks of history and over 1.25 million readings, while competing products claim much broader coverage. History alone creates no network effect or switching cost, and other trackers can start collecting the same public signals. The moat is conditional on authorized access plus differentiated coverage, accuracy, and retained history. (https://checkthecourse.com/ ; https://www.skoolstats.com/ ; https://playbuuk.com/)
build_effort: Medium-high, as an implementation estimate: confirm source permissions, build compliant source connectors and identity matching, store dated snapshots with citations, normalize prices and billing periods, monitor data quality, and deliver reports/API access with subscriptions and support. Avoid building an ingestion system around Skool until access rights are resolved. Existing trackers demonstrate the breadth of collection and reporting involved. (https://checkthecourse.com/methodology ; https://www.skoolanalytics.com/ ; https://www.skool.com/legal?t=terms)
channel: Use inbound SEO and public benchmark reports, listed data/API or integration marketplaces, opt-in partner listings, and paid ads configured for each target country’s rules. No cold email, SMS, DM, or calls; do not enrich or export owners’ contact details. The ICO says publicly available personal data still requires lawful handling and transparency. (https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/direct-marketing-guidance/collect-information-and-generate-leads/)
owner_hours_per_week: Estimated 3–5 hours in a stable, authorized, self-serve operation; unverified. Initial source clearance and build would exceed that target, and platform changes or data disputes could push ongoing work above it.
automation_reason: Estimated, not measured: agents could run permitted ingestion, deduplication, routine validation, report generation, billing administration, SEO publishing, and first-line support. Ricardo would still need to review permissions, anomalous data, privacy/takedown requests, and exceptions. This estimate assumes stable source access and a narrow product scope.
moat_assessment: Conditional data moat, not yet defensible. The proposed asset is valuable only if it is lawfully collectable and becomes broader, more accurate, or more useful over time than existing trackers. Direct incumbents already publish histories and benchmarks; no verified paid demand or customer switching cost was found. (https://checkthecourse.com/reports ; https://www.skoolanalytics.com/ ; https://www.skoolstats.com/ ; https://playbuuk.com/)
desk_test: Within one day, make a single honest sample report from a source whose terms clearly permit reuse, put it on a one-page inbound landing page with a stated paid-pilot offer, and list it only in marketplaces or public placements that allow promotion. Use a tightly capped, country-targeted search-ad test if immediate traffic is needed. Count paid pilot checkouts, not clicks or free signups; if authorized sample data is unavailable, test the concept without presenting fabricated figures.
red_flags: The lead now fails a deep-check as currently framed: the original data tracker already exists, several close substitutes are live, and the key Skool source’s published terms conflict with automated commercial collection. Competitor prices do not prove customer revenue, and no verified revenue, churn, API sales, or paid customer evidence was found. Proceed only after confirming lawful data access and getting a paid pilot commitment; otherwise the proposed data moat and revenue case remain unverified. (https://checkthecourse.com/ ; https://www.skool.com/legal?t=terms ; https://www.skoolstats.com/pricing ; https://www.skoolanalytics.com/)
